comparator.academicYear: Current published UvA bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The UvA markets the programme as Italië studies, while its official diploma is BA Italiaanse taal en cultuur and its RIO code is 56809, matching the normalized target. The published full-time pathway is 60+60+60=180 EC: year 1 includes four 6-EC Italian proficiency-and-culture courses and Italian language history; year 2 includes two further 6-EC Italian proficiency-and-culture courses, Italian film and identity study, and a 30-EC subject-linked semester in Italy; year 3 includes translation from Italian, Italy-specific identity study, a 12-EC thesis written in Italian, and 30 EC genuine free choice. The 30-EC abroad and open-choice components retain their published credit values without invented host courses or electives. The same curriculum can be taken part-time over more years; this reconstruction follows the standard full-time 180-EC structure.

exception.reason: The defining curriculum requires a progressive six-course Italian language-proficiency and culture sequence, Italian language history, translation from Italian, an Italy-specific study-abroad semester and an Italian-language subject thesis. The current UCR enriched catalogue has no Italian language instruction or advanced Italian-language reading, writing and translation sequence. A 24-course programme assembled from general European history, literary study, film, politics and Renaissance art would replace the core language and area-study progression rather than provide a defensible closest UCR match. The open 30 EC cannot compensate for the missing compulsory Italian-language core.
exception.curriculumContext: The published full-time curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: 60 EC in year one, 30 EC taught plus a 30-EC compulsory Italy-study semester in year two, and 18 EC taught plus a 12-EC Italian-language bachelor thesis and 30 EC genuine free choice in year three. Six successive 6-EC Italian proficiency-and-culture courses are compulsory across the first two years; history of Italian and translation add further language-specific work. No host courses or elective minor are inferred.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current enriched UCR course workbook, including descriptions, outlines, prerequisites and planned availability. MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean directly addresses Italian Renaissance art and Mediterranean connections, but is one 7.5-EC art-history course rather than a modern Italian studies or language sequence. MCCHEAM111 Introduction to Western Art History includes the Renaissance within a wider survey; MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works, MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning and MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media provide general literary or media methods. MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning analyses linguistic choices in literary and nonfiction texts, while HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics studies language processing; neither teaches Italian. GOSHIST111 Modern History provides broad European historical context. None supplies Italian grammar, oral and written proficiency, Italian-language source analysis, translation from Italian or a sustained modern-Italy curriculum. These adjacent courses cannot form a defensible 24-course closest match to the compulsory Italian-language and area-studies degree.
